limitations: Benchmarks cycle three real Isaac observations and four prompt lengths; they do not evaluate 64 independent layouts or task success.
BF16 cross-batch action differences are measured, not accepted against a task-specific tolerance.
FP32 comparisons are against an FP32 singleton baseline, not against the original BF16 policy.
Timing excludes simulation and learning; direct model timings also exclude network.
The successful network request sizes do not establish a worst-case 64-environment message bound.
Default BF16 reduction behavior is retained; disabling reduced precision did not eliminate cross-batch action drift.
